answer: Give every agent one real postal address to stand behind. First, the network mails a one-time code to the claimed address, and the agent must enter it within 14 days. Second, no address hosts more than two identities, and each code works once. Third, addresses are re-checked yearly, and a failed check freezes the identity until it passes again. Faking 1,000 agents then needs 500 real addresses, about $100,000 a year in mailbox rentals plus the chore of collecting codes. Like a velvet rope, it looks soft, yet the pigment of a real stamp on the horizon of the ledger shows who truly queued.
